verified_title: Action Images: End-to-End Policy Learning via Multiview Video Generation
problem: Abstract low-dimensional actions have weak spatial alignment with video priors, while converting generated motion back to metric control usually requires another learned inverse model.
contribution: Render7D EE pose/gripper commands as multiview RGB heatmaps, allowing a video generator to predict observation and action videos in one representation; decode control geometrically using calibrated cameras.
algorithm: Convert EE pose into position,up andnormal3Dpoints; project each into one RGB channel as a Gaussian, with binary gripper state in low-intensity blue background. Train masked flow matching for joint generation, action-conditioned video, video-to-action and video-only modes. Recover2D centroids, sample depth along a main-view ray, maximize side-view response, and reconstruct orientation from the3D axes. Camera Plücker embeddings condition generation.
observations: Language, initial multiview RGB and intrinsics/extrinsics; no online replanning in primary policy evaluation. Some uncalibrated data uses VGGT camera estimates; a metric scale anchor for safe physical reuse cannot be assumed from monocular geometry.
actions: 7D absolute EE position/orientation plus binary gripper, decoded from generated action images. This is Cartesian pose plus gripper, not a seven-joint arm command. Geometric decoder requires multiple views and valid camera projection; optional supervised MLP decoder is a separate stronger variant.
embodiment_and_data: DROID80k trajectories/two views; RLBench180k/four views with Robot-Colosseum augmentation; BridgeV2~30k used video-only because action/camera alignment is missing. Mixture20%Bridge/50%RLBench/30%DROID. Real zero-shot xArm uses unseen embodiment/objects/environment; held-out RLBench tasks remove only their RLBench examples, not all possible other-dataset occurrences.
experiments: Primary task success uses one-trial open-loop prediction, with nine zero-shot simulation/real tasks and nine in-domain RLBench tasks. Video metrics evaluate held-out videos; action reconstruction metrics are RLBench-only. Optional MLP and backbone/system optimizations are separate experiments. Training appendix reports32A100×100ksteps.
baselines: MV-DiffusionPolicy, camera-augmentedpi0.5, MolmoAct lifted multiview trajectories, and reproduced TesserAct/Cosmos-Policy on the authors' backbone/data. These are adaptations, not necessarily original official baseline checkpoints/configurations. Video-only comparisons include Cosmos-Predict, Tora, TAPIR andCoTracker.

quantitative_result.control: PDF p11 Table2: real zero-shot PlaceCup40%,PickToy20%,PickTissue15%,CloseDrawer45%,CloseBox10%; exact trial denominators NOT_EXTRACTED and not inferred from5-point increments. PDF p12 Table3: in-domain mean20.6% geometric decoder versus36.7% with extra supervised action head.
quantitative_result.reconstruction: PDF p12 Table4:3D error12.2×10^-3 versusTesserAct19.0×10^-3 on RLBench; dimensional unit is NOT_EXTRACTED, so not described as millimeters.
quantitative_result.compute: PDF p17 Table7: optimized5B variant2.3s for164 frames on8H100; approximately71 generated FPS is video throughput, not71Hz closed-loop control. Main text namesWan2.2; appendixp16 namesWan2.1-I2V-14B, while timing table names5B. Model-size/version inconsistency is unresolved.

limitations: Real success is modest, open-loop and denominator-uncertain. Reconstruction degrades with camera/scale errors, low resolution and ray discretization; raw reconstructed axes need geometric validity checks before an IK consumer. Eq7 uses background<0.25, while exactly encoded binary gripper1 puts background at0.25, potentially emptying the averaging set: an implementation boundary case to verify, not an observed executed failure. Learned-head gains show geometric decoding is not uniformly precise. Generated room examples and point-cloud trajectories do not establish real hardware success.
code_and_license: No pinned upstream code, model weights, license files or execution audited. Paper citations and apparent release intent do not establish reuse permissions; code/model/data terms UNKNOWN.
hardware_adaptation: COMPARE offline as a representation/decoder study. Pi's single overview camera lacks the required calibrated second view; M3/SO101 Cartesian reachability and binary/continuous gripper conventions need explicit adapters. First round-trip known feasible poses through rendered heatmaps and check metric errors, open/closed boundary behavior and rotation orthogonality. No evidence supports running the reported multi-H100 video model on NX at control rate.
